Glubczyce New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Głubczyce, Poland

Not demolished. Jewish settlement in Głubczyce likely began in the mid-14th century, though the community was expelled multiple times over the centuries. Population grew from 62 (1818) to 341 by 1890, then declined to 174 (1.3%) by 1910. Kristallnacht saw the synagogue burned and Jewish homes and shops plundered, with 10 arrests; by 1939 only 44 Jews remained before 1942 deportations to General Government ghettos. This newer cemetery, established July 1892, became Reich Association property in 1939 and Gestapo-controlled from 1943; its last burial occurred January 1941. Postwar destruction continued into the 1960s, when the funeral house was demolished and remaining matzevot stolen, likely repurposed for street paving.
